hook: Katti built his career on the unglamorous but essential problem of moving data efficiently, first in academic networking research, then running Intel's networking hardware division, and now at OpenAI, where the physical compute infrastructure behind frontier AI models is his direct responsibility.
name: Sachin Katti

quote.text: Compute is the substrate everything else in AI is built on; get the infrastructure wrong and nothing else matters.
quote.context: A recurring theme in Katti's public remarks on AI infrastructure strategy

moniker: OpenAI's Head of Compute and Former Stanford Networking Professor

reading.body:
Sachin Katti is the person at OpenAI directly responsible for the physical compute infrastructure that trains and serves its frontier models, a role he reached through an unusually straight career line from academic networking research to networking silicon to AI compute systems.

The pattern in his timeline is one of progressive scale. He studied how data moves efficiently in wireless systems at Stanford, then applied that thinking to networking hardware across an industrial hardware business at Intel, and then moved to OpenAI in 2024 to own the infrastructure layer where those same concerns, moving data fast and reliably between processors, become the binding constraint on what AI systems can do. His own public framing, that compute is the substrate everything else in AI is built on, aligns precisely with that trajectory.

What the data does not cover is the scope of the infrastructure he now oversees: cluster sizes, data center locations, power contracts, or hardware vendors are absent. His career record is documented through a Stanford faculty profile and an Intel newsroom item, so the sourcing is thin on the OpenAI period specifically. The record here establishes who he is and how he arrived at the role, not what decisions he has made inside it.
